newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures rebound late, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures rebound late, end mixed.

text.p: A strong rebound hoisted U.S. stock index futures to day's peaks and left them mixed.
The key June Standard & Poor's 500 futures contract snapped back from a hefty morning loss to a small daily gain during a spurt of busy afternoon buying and shortcovering.

Traders said the recovery, paced by dealer and bank buying that some said looked like new purchases, tugged S&Ps above resistance and triggered buystops, notably near 802.00 and again as the contract cleared last Friday's high at 805.30.
"We had good dealer buying....buy stops...then everybody and their brother came in and bought," said one floor broker.

They traced recovery in stock index futures to a similar bounce back in June U.S. Treasury bond futures, which recouped most of the morning's losses and hit Monday's pit-session peak at 108-24/32 during the final minutes of trade.

The snap back up in T-bond futures occurred on good volume as well, with dealers seen as size buyers after the June T-bond futures touched and respected the 108-07/32 - 06/32 area, roughly the key seven-percent cash yield equivalent.
The return higher in stocks also attracted arbitrage buy programs, as the premium widened past fair value of about 7.70 points over cash for June futures, brokers said.

Earlier in the session, stock index futures had slumped in tandem with erosion in T-bond futures, and June S&Ps skidded below key support at 796.50-20 and 794.70 and to a loss of some 13.00 points despite their extremely oversold condition.
Arbitrage sell programs were apparent on the decline as the premium over cash collapsed, brokers said.
But the contract managed to halt its decline above trendline support at 789.00, which encouraged shortcovering.
Some brokers tied early losses to a New York Times article that said Warren Buffett in his annual Berkshire Hathaway shareholders letter said most U.S. stocks were overvalued.
June Nikkei futures briefly probed above resistance at 18,000 but backed down and ended slightly below there
Nikkei futures firmed early in response to Japan's higher year-on-year customs-cleared trade surplus, which grew 6.5 percent in February, the first rise in two years.

June S&P 500s rose 1.40 pts to 804.40, Value Lines dipped 1.95 to 721.25, Nikkei rose 40.0 to 18,040.0, Midcap 400s lost 3.80 to 265.00, NYSE composite firmed 0.40 to 422.80, Russell 2000 lost 4.40 to 360.0, and Nasdaq 100 fell 4.75 to 846.00.
